reference.notes:
I implemented `limitJobs` in `apps/worker/src/evaluation/limit.ts`, and every test passes: 60/60 in `limit-jobs-check`, 74/74 in `hidden-limit-jobs-check`, and 254/254 in the whole worker suite. I changed no other file.

How it works:
- **Taking a slot:** each `limitJobs` call keeps its own count of held slots and its own queue of waiting callers. A create takes a free slot right away (free means `held < max`, with no check on `max`). The real `provider.create` is called on a later microtask, and it is called on the provider object itself, so providers built as classes still work.
- **Errors from create:** if the real create throws or rejects, either way, the slot is released and the same error is passed on to the caller.
- **Waiting and aborts:** a caller that has to wait and whose signal is already aborted rejects with `signal.reason` without joining the queue. A waiter whose signal aborts later leaves the queue and rejects with `signal.reason`. When a slot is handed to a waiter, its abort listener is removed, so a later abort is left to the real provider.
- **The wrapped job:** it is a new object with only `id`, `environment`, `stage`, `exec`, `read` and `destroy`, each passed straight through. `destroy` always calls the real `destroy`, but releases the slot only once, when the first call settles, whether it succeeds or throws. A freed slot goes to the oldest waiter if there is one.
- **The wrapped provider:** it has only `name` (the real provider's name) and `create`.

As the spec allows, I did not wire `limitJobs` into `apps/worker/src/main.ts`, and nothing is committed.
